boards.school_name: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
boards.description: Ten food-focused destinations with current late closing times in the East Village and nearby downtown Manhattan.

cards.title: Taqueria Diana
cards.subtitle: 129 2nd Ave, East Village
cards.notes: Check the day before heading out: the East Village location lists food service until 1am–4am, depending on the day.
cards.short_summary: A nearby taco counter with especially late weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taqueria Diana lists its East Village address at 129 2nd Ave and hours through 1am Sunday–Monday, 2am Tuesday–Wednesday, 3am Thursday, and 4am Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists late hours; confirm before travel because schedules can change.

cards.title: Nuovo York Pizza
cards.subtitle: 105 E 9th St, East Village
cards.notes: Use the posted late-night window for a straightforward pizza stop; the restaurant lists closing at 3am or 4:30am.
cards.short_summary: East Village pizza with nightly late closing.
cards.evidence_claim: Nuovo York Pizza lists 105 E 9th St and hours of 11am–3am Monday–Thursday and Sunday, plus 11am–4:30am Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site says it is open late every night, with service until 3am or 4:30am.

cards.title: Maza Cloud Kitchens
cards.subtitle: 102 E 7th St, East Village
cards.notes: Keep this one for delivery or takeout planning: its official page posts service through 1am on weekdays and 2am Friday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A delivery- and takeout-first East Village kitchen with late hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Maza Cloud Kitchens lists 102 E 7th St and delivery/takeout hours until 1am Monday–Thursday and 2am Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site specifies delivery and takeout service through 1am weekdays and 2am Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Empanada Mama
cards.subtitle: 95 Allen St, Lower East Side
cards.notes: For an overnight option a little south of campus, use the Lower East Side location, not the earlier-closing East Village branch.
cards.short_summary: An all-night Lower East Side empanada stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Empanada Mama lists its Lower East Side location at 95 Allen St as open 24/7.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists the Lower East Side restaurant as open 24/7.

cards.title: Veselka
cards.subtitle: 144 2nd Ave, East Village
cards.notes: Use the East Village location page to match your night: it lists midnight on weekdays and overnight or 24-hour service across the weekend.
cards.short_summary: Ukrainian food with extended East Village weekend service.
cards.evidence_claim: Veselka lists its East Village restaurant at 144 2nd Ave, open until midnight Monday–Thursday, overnight Friday, 24 hours Saturday, and until 11pm Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page posts late and overnight weekend availability; verify the specific day before leaving.

cards.title: 7th Street Burger
cards.subtitle: 91 E 7th St, East Village
cards.notes: Check the daily schedule before walking over; this location lists 1am closes early week and 3am Thursday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A made-to-order burger and fries counter with late East Village hours.
cards.evidence_claim: 7th Street Burger lists its East Village location at 91 E 7th St, open until 1am Monday–Wednesday, 3am Thursday–Saturday, and 2am Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists closing times from 1am to 3am, varying by day.

cards.title: Café Standard
cards.subtitle: The Standard, East Village, 25 Cooper Sq
cards.notes: This is the closest late sit-down option on the hotel block: use the all-day menu hours, which run to 11pm or midnight.
cards.short_summary: A Cooper Square hotel café with late all-day dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The Standard, East Village lists Café Standard at 25 Cooper Sq with all-day hours until 11pm Sunday–Thursday and midnight Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hotel dining page lists the café's all-day service through 11pm or midnight.

cards.title: Pommes Frites
cards.subtitle: 128 MacDougal St, Greenwich Village
cards.notes: Plan around the weekend schedule: the official menu lists fries until midnight Sunday–Thursday and until 2am Friday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: Belgian-style fries with late Greenwich Village weekend service.
cards.evidence_claim: Pommes Frites lists 128 MacDougal St and hours until midnight Sunday–Thursday and 2am Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists closing at midnight most nights and 2am Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Crif Dogs
cards.subtitle: 113 St Marks Pl, East Village
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s posted late window for a food stop on St. Marks Place: it lists 2am most nights and 3am Friday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: An East Village hot-dog restaurant open into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Crif Dogs lists its East Village restaurant at 113 St Marks Pl as open until 2am Sunday–Thursday and 3am Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Crif Dogs — East Village Hours and Location
cards.access_notes: Official location page says “Open Late Daily” and posts 2am or 3am closing times.

cards.title: Mamoun's Falafel
cards.subtitle: 119 MacDougal St, Greenwich Village
cards.notes: This Greenwich Village location offers a later fallback than the East Village branch; its posted closing time ranges from 1am to 4am.
cards.short_summary: A Greenwich Village falafel counter with the board's latest listed closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Mamoun's Falafel lists its Greenwich Village location at 119 MacDougal St, open until 2am Monday–Wednesday, 3am Thursday, 4am Friday–Saturday, and 1am Sunday.
cards.source_title: Mamoun's Falafel — Greenwich Village Hours and Location
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists service until 1am–4am depending on the day.

boards.school_name: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Named Cooper Union spaces for making, viewing work, studying, and attending campus gatherings.

cards.title: Prototype in the Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Room 707, 41 Cooper Square
cards.notes: Bring a class or learning-focused project, ask an operator for help, and use the prototyping tools or submit a 3D-print request.
cards.short_summary: A staffed prototyping lab with tools and support for student projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Makerspace is in Room 707 at 41 Cooper Square; its FAQ describes it as a prototyping lab and says learning-focused student materials and services are free.
cards.access_notes: Availability follows the Makerspace’s posted schedule; class projects receive priority.

cards.title: Settle into the Cooper Union Library
cards.subtitle: First floor, Foundation Building
cards.notes: Use the library for research and focused reading, then ask library staff about its collections and reciprocal-library access.
cards.short_summary: The campus library anchors research support in the Foundation Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union identifies its library on the Foundation Building’s first floor and lists its research collections and reciprocal access arrangements.
cards.source_title: School of Art Facilities and Resources
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current schedule before visiting; building access may be limited to the Cooper community.

cards.title: Attend a Great Hall program
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building, 7 East 7th Street
cards.notes: Watch the university calendar for lectures, ceremonies, or public programs held in this historic gathering space.
cards.short_summary: A historic Cooper Union venue for campus milestones and civic conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union describes the Great Hall in the Foundation Building as a place of meet-ups, milestones, and ceremony for generations of Cooper students.
cards.source_title: Great Hall History Comes Alive in New Digital Archive
cards.access_notes: Program access varies by event; consult the hosting event’s details.

cards.title: See work at 41 Cooper Gallery
cards.subtitle: 41 Cooper Square
cards.notes: Check the student-exhibition calendar, then visit to see senior, class, exchange, or fellowship work when it is on display.
cards.short_summary: A 41 Cooper Square gallery used for student and school exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union says gallery spaces at 41 Cooper Square showcase graduating seniors’ work as well as exchange, class-project, and fellowship work.
cards.source_title: School of Art Facilities and Resources
cards.access_notes: Exhibition dates and public access vary; verify the current show calendar.

cards.title: Work through a Media Lab project
cards.subtitle: Rooms 804–806, eighth floor, 41 Cooper Square
cards.notes: Use the digital workstations, printers, scanners, and technical support when preparing class materials or media-production projects.
cards.short_summary: A digital workspace with output equipment and staff support.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union describes the Media Lab as an open workspace in rooms 804–806 with iMacs, printers, scanners, production software, and technical support.
cards.source_title: School of Art Facilities and Resources
cards.access_notes: Resources are for Cooper Union students, faculty, and staff; ask staff about equipment use.

cards.entity_name: Herb Lubalin Study Center of Design and Typography
cards.title: Browse design history at Lubalin
cards.subtitle: Room LL119, 41 Cooper Square
cards.notes: Make an appointment to consult the design archive, then look for public exhibitions or lectures that draw from its collection.
cards.short_summary: A design-history study center, library, and archive within 41 Cooper.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union says the Herb Lubalin Study Center preserves design history through its core collection, library, and archive, with materials available by appointment.
cards.source_title: School of Art Facilities and Resources
cards.access_notes: Archive materials are available by appointment; exhibition and lecture access varies.

cards.title: Make a plan for the AACE Lab
cards.subtitle: Room 400, Foundation Building
cards.notes: Bring a fabrication idea, review the lab’s available equipment, and coordinate with staff before beginning a digital-fabrication task.
cards.short_summary: A campus fabrication resource serving current Cooper Union students.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union identifies the AACE Lab in Foundation Building Room 400 as an advanced digital-fabrication resource for current students.
cards.access_notes: Use is for current students; follow lab staff guidance and equipment safety requirements.

cards.title: Catch a Rose Auditorium gathering
cards.subtitle: 41 Cooper Square
cards.notes: Look for Student Affairs and academic events scheduled here, and arrive with time to find the room before the program begins.
cards.short_summary: A 41 Cooper Square auditorium used for orientation and campus programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union’s 2025–2026 orientation schedule lists Rose Auditorium at 41 Cooper Square as the location for a Student Affairs session.
cards.access_notes: Access depends on the scheduled program and its audience.

cards.title: Work from a Foundation Building studio
cards.subtitle: Second, fourth, and sixth floors, Foundation Building
cards.notes: If assigned a studio, use its desk, pinup wall, and storage to develop work and prepare for critiques or presentations.
cards.short_summary: Assigned art-student studios with practical space for ongoing work.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union says second-, third-, and fourth-year art students and exchange students receive individual studio spaces, including on floors two, four, and six of the Foundation Building.
cards.source_title: School of Art Facilities and Resources
cards.access_notes: Individual studios are assigned to eligible School of Art and exchange students.

cards.title: Use the Foundation Building as a campus anchor
cards.subtitle: 7 East 7th Street, between Third and Fourth Avenues
cards.notes: Orient yourself to the building’s library, Great Hall, studios, and academic spaces before heading across Third Avenue to 41 Cooper.
cards.short_summary: Cooper Union’s landmark building concentrates several academic and gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union identifies the Foundation Building at 7 East 7th Street and its architecture materials list it as home to art and architecture programs, the Great Hall, and the library.
cards.access_notes: Check Cooper Union’s building-hours information and any event-specific access instructions.

boards.school_name: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten public, under-21-safe cultural stops with verified free exhibitions, displays, or library programming.

cards.entity_name: Polonsky Exhibition of The New York Public Library's Treasures
cards.title: Browse NYPL’s Treasures
cards.subtitle: Gottesman Hall, Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
cards.notes: Meet at Gottesman Hall, choose a few objects to inspect together, then compare the stories or details that caught everyone’s attention.
cards.short_summary: An ongoing free exhibition of remarkable items from NYPL’s collections.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL identifies the Polonsky Exhibition as an ongoing, fully accessible free exhibition in Gottesman Hall.
cards.source_title: Polonsky Exhibition of The New York Public Library's Treasures
cards.access_notes: Public exhibition; NYPL notes that final daily entry is 30 minutes before the building closes.

cards.title: Listen Through the Treasures Audio Guide
cards.subtitle: Polonsky Exhibition, Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
cards.notes: Bring headphones and pick one guide theme as a group. Pause at a shared highlight before moving on to the next case.
cards.short_summary: A free onsite or mobile audio guide for NYPL’s ongoing Treasures exhibition.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL offers a free Treasures Audio Guide that is accessible onsite or from a visitor’s mobile device.
cards.source_title: Polonsky Exhibition of The New York Public Library's Treasures
cards.access_notes: Bring headphones for the mobile guide; the exhibition is listed as fully accessible.

cards.title: See “Declaring America”
cards.subtitle: Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
cards.notes: Plan a gallery stop around one question about how the documents and objects frame the country’s 250th anniversary.
cards.short_summary: A current NYPL exhibition running June 15, 2026 through January 10, 2027.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL lists Declaring America: 1776 and Beyond at the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building from June 15, 2026 to January 10, 2027; NYPL states its major exhibitions are free.
cards.access_notes: NYPL describes its research-library exhibitions as free; confirm building hours before traveling.

cards.title: Catch a Free Library Program
cards.subtitle: Ottendorfer Library, East Village
cards.notes: Use NYPL’s calendar to choose a no-cost program, arrive a few minutes early, and make the post-event walk part of the plan.
cards.short_summary: NYPL offers free events, programs, classes, and book clubs at its locations.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL states that its locations offer a wide array of free events, programs, classes, book clubs, and more.
cards.access_notes: Check the calendar’s current Ottendorfer listing for format, audience, registration, and timing.

cards.entity_name: Free program at Tompkins Square Library
cards.title: Make a Library Event Plan
cards.subtitle: Tompkins Square Library, East Village
cards.notes: Pick a free program from the library calendar and use the event as a low-key reason to reconnect with classmates or neighbors.
cards.short_summary: A public-library program option with no admission or purchase required.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL says its event calendar covers free events, programs, classes, book clubs, and more at its locations.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current Tompkins Square Library listing before going; program formats and registration can vary.

cards.entity_name: Free program at Jefferson Market Library
cards.title: Join a Free NYPL Gathering
cards.subtitle: Jefferson Market Library, Greenwich Village
cards.notes: Choose a current calendar listing with friends, then leave room afterward to trade notes on the speaker, book, film, or activity.
cards.short_summary: NYPL’s public calendar includes free programs and community-oriented events.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL states that it offers thousands of free programs each year, including author talks, performances, exhibitions, and classes.
cards.access_notes: Use NYPL’s current calendar to verify a Jefferson Market program’s time, location, and any registration requirement.

cards.entity_name: Free program at Seward Park Library
cards.title: Set Up a Free Library Stop
cards.subtitle: Seward Park Library, Lower East Side
cards.notes: Find a current program on NYPL’s calendar, make it the meetup anchor, and keep the plan flexible for whatever format is listed.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost public program option at an NYPL location.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL describes its event offerings as free and includes programs, classes, book clubs, performances, and exhibitions.
cards.access_notes: Check the live calendar for Seward Park Library before heading out; availability and program details change.

cards.entity_name: Free program at Mulberry Street Library
cards.title: Try a Free Library Class or Talk
cards.subtitle: Mulberry Street Library, Little Italy
cards.notes: Browse the current calendar together, select a free listing that fits the group, and confirm whether it is in-person, online, or outdoors.
cards.short_summary: NYPL’s calendar groups free classes, talks, performances, and other events.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL states that its event calendar provides free events, programs, classes, book clubs, and more.
cards.access_notes: Verify the current Mulberry Street Library program listing and any registration directions before attending.

cards.entity_name: Free program at Hudson Park Library
cards.title: Meet at a Free NYPL Program
cards.subtitle: Hudson Park Library, West Village
cards.notes: Use the calendar to find a no-cost event, agree on a meeting point outside, and give yourselves time to settle in before it begins.
cards.short_summary: A free public-program option at an NYPL branch.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL says that its locations host thousands of free programs a year, including talks, performances, exhibitions, and classes.
cards.access_notes: Consult NYPL’s current listings for Hudson Park Library; timing, attendance rules, and format are event-specific.

cards.entity_name: Free program at Chatham Square Library
cards.title: Build a No-Cost Library Hang
cards.subtitle: Chatham Square Library, Chinatown
cards.notes: Choose one currently listed free event as the centerpiece, then make space afterward to discuss what you learned or made together.
cards.short_summary: NYPL’s public events span free book clubs, classes, talks, performances, and exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL states that it provides thousands of free programs annually across its locations.
cards.access_notes: Check the NYPL calendar for a currently scheduled Chatham Square Library event and any sign-up instructions.

boards.school_name: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named Cooper Union spaces for research, writing, design, and project work, with access limits noted where published.

cards.title: The Cooper Union Library
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Start with the physical collections or an individual research task. Check the current library schedule before heading over, especially for weekend work.
cards.short_summary: A campus library with specialized collections and computer facilities for individual research and study.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper says its Library is on the first floor of the Foundation Building, holds specialized collections, and has computer facilities for individual research and study.
cards.source_title: Facilities and Resources | The Cooper Union
cards.access_notes: Official page lists class-session library hours: Mon–Thu 8:30am–9pm, Fri 8:30am–6pm, Sat 1–5pm, Sun 1–9pm.

cards.title: Cooper Union Library Atrium
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building library
cards.notes: Use the atrium for collaborative reading or a project conversation. Keep plans flexible when a library talk or club meeting is scheduled there.
cards.short_summary: An updated library gathering area documented with tables for collaborative project work.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper describes the renovated Library atrium as hosting club meetings and faculty talks, with tables encircled by students collaborating on projects.
cards.source_title: Space for Renewal | The Cooper Union
cards.access_notes: Located within the Library; library hours are listed on Cooper's facilities page. Events may affect use.

cards.title: Center for Writing and Learning
cards.subtitle: Inside the Cooper Union Library
cards.notes: Bring a draft or assignment question and use the center alongside nearby research materials. Confirm appointment or drop-in procedures directly with the center.
cards.short_summary: A writing-support space integrated into the campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper states that the Center for Writing and Learning is within the Library and offers support to students and faculty.
cards.source_title: Facilities and Resources | The Cooper Union School of Architecture
cards.access_notes: Cooper identifies the center as being within the Library; verify current consultation procedures before visiting.

cards.title: Architecture Study Collection
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building, 7th Floor
cards.notes: Choose this for architecture references that do not circulate. Plan to work on site and ask library or archive staff about handling requirements.
cards.short_summary: A seventh-floor collection of non-circulating architecture books.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper says the Architecture Study Collection is on the seventh floor and contains non-circulating books not otherwise available in the Library.
cards.access_notes: Materials are non-circulating; consult the Library or Architecture Archive for current on-site access procedures.

cards.title: School of Architecture Archive
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building
cards.notes: Request rare books, magazines, portfolios, or films for course research. Contact the archive ahead when your work needs a particular item or viewing setup.
cards.short_summary: An archive with rare and audiovisual architecture resources for student and faculty use.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper says the Architecture Archive holds films, rare books, magazines, and limited-edition portfolios for student and faculty use.
cards.access_notes: The archive's other resources page says films can be viewed in the office by appointment; ask staff about access to other materials.

cards.entity_name: The Paul Laux Digital Architecture Studio
cards.title: The Paul Laux Digital Architecture Studio
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building, 7th Floor, Rooms 713–714
cards.notes: Use a workstation for rendering, coding, scanning, or print preparation. Save work externally and ask lab staff when you need software or hardware help.
cards.short_summary: A full-service computer lab with design software, render stations, and project-production tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper identifies the Paul Laux Digital Architecture Studio as a full-service computer lab and classroom open to all Cooper students, faculty, and staff.
cards.source_title: IT Labs: The Paul Laux Digital Architecture Studio | The Cooper Union
cards.access_notes: Official access is for Cooper students, faculty, and staff. The published page lists Spring 2022 hours; verify current hours with the lab.

cards.title: The Media Lab
cards.subtitle: 41 Cooper Square, 8th Floor
cards.notes: Set up digital project work here when you need Apple desktops, scanning, printing, or 3D tools. Ask the staffed lab for current availability.
cards.short_summary: An eighth-floor computer lab supporting graphic, video, coding, and 3D coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper says the Media Lab on the eighth floor of 41 Cooper Square is a full-service computer lab and classroom open to all Cooper students, faculty, and staff.
cards.source_title: Shops & Labs | The Cooper Union School of Architecture
cards.access_notes: Official access is for Cooper students, faculty, and staff; check directly with the lab for current hours and equipment availability.

cards.title: The Herb Lubalin Study Center
cards.subtitle: 41 Cooper Square
cards.notes: Visit with a focused visual-research question and allow time to examine the study materials. Confirm current visitor and collection-access arrangements before going.
cards.short_summary: A named study center housed at 41 Cooper Square.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper's campus history page lists the Herb Lubalin Study Center among the facilities housed at 41 Cooper Square.
cards.access_notes: Cooper identifies the location but does not publish access procedures on this page; contact the school before visiting.

cards.title: Architecture Studio
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Architecture students can use their assigned desk for extended model, drawing, and desk-based work. Treat the studio as assigned academic space and follow program rules.
cards.short_summary: A large third-floor open studio with individual student workspaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper's published open-house material states that School of Architecture students have individual workspace in a single 8,000-square-foot open studio on the Foundation Building's third floor.
cards.access_notes: Workspace is described for School of Architecture students; it is not represented as general drop-in seating.

cards.entity_name: IDC Foundation Art, Architecture, Construction, and Engineering Lab
cards.title: IDC Foundation AACE Lab
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building, 4th Floor
cards.notes: Use the lab for a fabrication-focused research or design session after required training. Bring a defined project and consult technicians about safe equipment use.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor, interdisciplinary maker facility for student fabrication and project development.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper says the AACE Lab is a high-tech maker facility for students from all three schools, housed in a former fourth-floor lobby of the Foundation Building.
cards.source_title: One Lab for All | The Cooper Union
cards.access_notes: Cooper describes the lab as open for in-person student use and self-service; use is subject to training, safety requirements, and lab procedures.

boards.school_name: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named cultural, civic, and book-oriented destinations on the corridors around Cooper Union.

cards.title: See the kinetic cube
cards.subtitle: Astor Place, beside Lafayette Street
cards.notes: Walk the plaza and look at Tony Rosenthal’s kinetic steel cube from several angles; the City accepted Alamo as a permanent public artwork.
cards.short_summary: A permanent kinetic sculpture at Astor Place.
cards.evidence_claim: NYC Parks’ public-art history identifies Tony Rosenthal’s kinetic painted-steel cube, Alamo, at Astor Place and says it was accepted permanently by the City.
cards.source_title: 40 Years of Public Art in New York City Parks
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public artwork at Astor Place.

cards.title: Check the current stage calendar
cards.subtitle: Lafayette Street at Astor Place
cards.notes: Check the current calendar before heading over, then choose a production at The Public’s landmark Astor Place home on Lafayette Street.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit theater with new-work programming at Astor Place.
cards.evidence_claim: The Public Theater says its programming includes an annual season of new work at its landmark home at Astor Place, 425 Lafayette Street.
cards.access_notes: See the official calendar and ticket details for a specific production.

cards.title: Browse Broadway’s book stacks
cards.subtitle: Broadway between 12th Street and 4th Avenue
cards.notes: Use the store’s category browsing to pick a section, then visit the 828 Broadway shop with the seller entrance by 12th Street.
cards.short_summary: A bookshop located at 828 Broadway.
cards.evidence_claim: Strand Books lists its location as 828 Broadway, with the seller entrance at 12th Street between Broadway and Fourth Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Retail browsing is available; confirm store information before traveling.

cards.title: Follow East 4th Street to new work
cards.subtitle: East 4th Street at 74A
cards.notes: Review the season and reserve only if a performance fits your schedule; the renovated building includes two intimate performance spaces and community space.
cards.short_summary: An experimental-theater destination in a renovated landmark building.
cards.evidence_claim: La MaMa says its 74A East 4th Street building was renovated with two intimate performance spaces, an enlarged lobby, accessibility, and community space.
cards.access_notes: See La MaMa’s official listings for program-specific tickets and access details.

cards.title: Enter an 1832 house museum
cards.subtitle: East 4th Street at 29
cards.notes: Plan a timed museum visit to see the late-Federal exterior and Greek Revival interiors in a house recognized as a National Historic Landmark.
cards.short_summary: A preserved 19th-century house museum on East 4th Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Merchant’s House Museum identifies 29 East Fourth Street as a National Historic Landmark with an 1832 late-Federal exterior and Greek Revival interior rooms.
cards.access_notes: Consult the museum’s current visit information before going.

cards.title: Use a historic public library
cards.subtitle: Second Avenue at 135, near East 8th Street
cards.notes: Bring a book or use the reading area and computers; NYPL describes this 1884 branch as New York City’s first free public library.
cards.short_summary: An 1884 NYPL branch with public-library resources.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL says Ottendorfer Library opened in 1884 as New York City’s first free public library and offers books, Wi-Fi, computers, classes, and programs.
cards.source_title: Ottendorfer Library | The New York Public Library
cards.access_notes: NYPL lists the address as 135 Second Avenue; check the location page for current hours.

cards.title: See the exhibition program
cards.subtitle: East 6th Street at 222, between Second and Third avenues
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition listings, then allow time for the galleries at the museum’s East 6th Street building and its arts-and-culture guide.
cards.short_summary: A museum with changing exhibitions on East 6th Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ukrainian Museum lists changing exhibitions and identifies its location as 222 East 6th Street.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists public hours of noon–6 PM and closure Monday–Tuesday; verify before visiting.

cards.title: Read the independent-film calendar
cards.subtitle: Second Avenue at East 2nd Street
cards.notes: Scan the official calendar for a screening, then head to the archive’s Second Avenue venue; its site lists daily programs and ticket links.
cards.short_summary: An archive and screening venue for independent and artist-made cinema.
cards.evidence_claim: Anthology Film Archives lists its Second Avenue address, a film calendar, programs, collections, and ticket links.
cards.access_notes: Check the official calendar for screening times and ticket availability.

cards.title: Find the Hare Krishna Tree
cards.subtitle: Avenue B at East 10th Street
cards.notes: Walk to the central plaza and locate the Hare Krishna Tree, an American elm identified by NYC Parks; the park also has mapped trees and events.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood park with a named historic elm in its central plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: NYC Parks identifies Tompkins Square Park’s Hare Krishna Tree as an American elm in the central plaza and lists 343 mapped trees.
cards.source_title: Tompkins Square Park Great Trees | NYC Parks
cards.access_notes: NYC Parks identifies the park as a 10.50-acre neighborhood park; check park notices before visiting.

cards.title: Time a walk for market day
cards.subtitle: Union Square West and 17th Street, off Broadway
cards.notes: Go on a listed market day to browse regional farmers, fishers, and bakers; GrowNYC also publishes producer maps and compost drop-off hours.
cards.short_summary: A year-round farmers market with scheduled market days.
cards.evidence_claim: GrowNYC lists Union Square Greenmarket as year-round on Monday, Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday, at 17th Street between Broadway and Park Avenue South.
cards.access_notes: Market hours listed by GrowNYC are 8 AM–6 PM on Monday, Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday; verify daily producer attendance.

boards.school_name: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Cooper Union rituals and recurring campus practices, from the founder’s birthday wreath to the year-end robot ring.

cards.title: Lay a wreath for the founder
cards.subtitle: Peter Cooper statue, Cooper Square
cards.notes: Look for the February observance of Peter Cooper’s birthday, when the Cooper community gathers and a wreath is placed at his statue.
cards.short_summary: A winter founder’s-birthday observance centered on the Peter Cooper statue.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union documented students, faculty, alumni, and staff gathering on February 11 to mark Peter Cooper’s birthday and placing a wreath at the statue “following tradition.”
cards.source_title: In Spite of Obstacles, Peter Cooper Gets His Birthday Wreath
cards.access_notes: This is a recurring observance; consult the institution’s events calendar for any future public details.

cards.entity_name: Cooper Union Alumni Association Founder’s Day Awards
cards.title: Mark Founder’s Day with alumni awards
cards.subtitle: Cooper Together / Cooper Union Alumni Association
cards.notes: Follow the annual Founder’s Day awards announcement to see alumni recognized across Cooper’s art, architecture, engineering, and service communities.
cards.short_summary: An annual February celebration recognizing Cooper alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union states that each February it honors alumni accomplishments in an annual Founder’s Day award celebration.
cards.source_title: Founder's Day Award Reception honors Alumni Leaders
cards.access_notes: The 2025 ceremony required advance registration and charged a fee; future arrangements may differ.

cards.title: Turn the campus into a gallery
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building and 41 Cooper Square
cards.notes: Visit the annual End of Year Show to see culminating architecture, art, and engineering projects spread through studios, galleries, lobbies, and hallways.
cards.short_summary: A Cooper-wide public showcase that remakes academic spaces into exhibition space.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union describes the End of Year Show as an annual public exhibition of student work across architecture, art, and engineering.
cards.source_title: 2026 End of Year Show: Photos from Opening Night
cards.access_notes: The 2025 show was free and open to the public; check the current exhibition page for dates and entry details.

cards.title: Read the art show’s artist-only labels
cards.subtitle: End of Year Show, School of Art
cards.notes: At the End of Year Show, notice that School of Art works identify the artist without the usual additional program notation.
cards.short_summary: A documented attribution convention within Cooper’s annual student exhibition.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union says School of Art works at the End of Year Show are identified only by the artist, “per tradition.”
cards.source_title: 2026 End of Year Show: Photos from Opening Night
cards.access_notes: See this convention within the End of Year Show; individual exhibition access varies by year.

cards.title: Find the architecture work credited to a studio
cards.subtitle: End of Year Show, Irwin S. Chanin School of Architecture
cards.notes: When viewing architecture projects at the End of Year Show, read the studio attribution rather than expecting an individual author credit.
cards.short_summary: Architecture exhibition work follows a studio-based attribution convention.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union says End of Year Show works from its School of Architecture are attributed to the studio in which they were created, with no specific author.
cards.source_title: 2026 End of Year Show: Photos from Opening Night
cards.access_notes: See this convention within the End of Year Show; individual exhibition access varies by year.

cards.entity_name: End of Year Show Robot Sumo Competition
cards.title: Cheer for autonomous Robot Sumo
cards.subtitle: End of Year Show, Mechatronics course
cards.notes: Watch for the annual Robot Sumo ring during the End of Year Show, where autonomous robots made in the mechatronics course compete.
cards.short_summary: An annual autonomous-robot contest staged as part of Cooper’s year-end exhibition.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union identifies Robot Sumo as an annual End of Year Show competition featuring autonomous robots designed in its mechatronics course.
cards.source_title: 2026 End of Year Show: Photos from Opening Night
cards.access_notes: Presented as part of the annual End of Year Show; consult that year’s program for scheduling.

cards.entity_name: Benjamin Menschel Fellowship Exhibition and Gala
cards.title: See Menschel fellows present their work
cards.subtitle: Benjamin Menschel Fellowship Program
cards.notes: Browse the annual Menschel Fellowship exhibition and its catalog to encounter interdisciplinary student research projects from the prior fellowship year.
cards.short_summary: A yearly exhibition and gala documenting student fellowship projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union states that the Benjamin Menschel Fellowship program culminates in an annual exhibition and gala opening, accompanied by a student-contributed catalog.
cards.access_notes: The archive records exhibitions since 1999; check the fellowship program for current exhibition information.

cards.entity_name: The Mace of The Cooper Union
cards.title: Spot the mace leading the procession
cards.subtitle: Commencement academic procession
cards.notes: At commencement, look for Cooper’s symbolic mace at the head of the academic procession and read its science-and-art design meaning.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial mace leads every Cooper Union academic procession.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union states that its mace, emblematic of the president’s authority and responsibility, is carried at the head of all academic processions.
cards.access_notes: Part of formal academic processions; attendance and guest procedures are set for each commencement.

cards.title: Graduate in the Great Hall
cards.subtitle: The Great Hall, Foundation Building
cards.notes: Notice the setting at commencement: Cooper holds the ceremony in the historic Great Hall, tying graduates to a long public-program legacy.
cards.short_summary: A commencement ritual staged in Cooper’s historic public-forum space.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union’s 2026 home page says its 166th Commencement was held in the historic Great Hall.
cards.source_title: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
cards.access_notes: Commencement is a formal institutional event; follow the current commencement page for guest details.

cards.title: Build through Hack Cooper
cards.subtitle: Create@Cooper student-run community
cards.notes: Look for Hack Cooper, Create@Cooper’s annual 24-hour hackathon, for a documented student-run format focused on making and presenting projects.
cards.short_summary: A recurring student-run hackathon connected to Cooper’s maker community.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Union describes Hack Cooper as an annual 24-hour hackathon organized by the student-run Create@Cooper community.
cards.access_notes: Event format, registration, and participation details are set by Create@Cooper for each edition.

boards.school_name: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art
boards.title: Your First Weekend at The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend loop that starts on campus, adds nearby public study and outdoor stops, and leaves room to check Cooper’s current events calendar.

cards.title: Begin at Astor Place Plaza
cards.subtitle: Public plaza on Astor Place, from Fourth Avenue to Cooper Square
cards.notes: Meet your group at the tables and chairs, orient yourself to the surrounding streets, then use the plaza as the starting point for the campus loop.
cards.short_summary: A furnished public plaza immediately beside Cooper Square.
cards.evidence_claim: NYC DOT lists Astor Place Plaza on Astor Place from Fourth Avenue to Cooper Square; the City says it has daily-use tables, chairs, and umbrellas.
cards.access_notes: City describes daily-use furniture; follow posted rules and any event setup.

cards.title: Find the Foundation Building entrance
cards.subtitle: 7 East 7th Street, between Third and Fourth Avenues
cards.notes: Locate the historic academic building and its security desk first; it anchors the library, galleries, studios, classrooms, and Great Hall.
cards.short_summary: Cooper’s landmark original academic building.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper identifies the Foundation Building at 7 East 7th Street and says it contains classrooms, studios, the library, the Arthur A. Houghton Jr. Gallery, and the Great Hall.
cards.access_notes: Students enter academic buildings by swiping a current Cooper ID during posted building hours.

cards.title: Settle in at the Cooper Union Library
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building, 7 East 7th Street
cards.notes: Bring your Cooper ID, find the library on your first pass through the building, and note the Center for Writing and Learning nearby.
cards.short_summary: A campus library and writing-support location.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper says its Library is on the first floor of the Foundation Building and that the Center for Writing and Learning is located within it.
cards.access_notes: The library serves Cooper students, faculty, and staff; confirm desk and service availability before arriving.

cards.title: Check the Great Hall calendar
cards.subtitle: Foundation Building, 7 East 7th Street
cards.notes: Look for an upcoming public program or lecture, then plan around its listed registration and arrival instructions rather than assuming drop-in access.
cards.short_summary: Cooper’s historic auditorium and public-program venue.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper identifies the Great Hall in the Foundation Building and documents it as a venue for public programs and events.
cards.source_title: Great Hall History Comes Alive in New Digital Archive
cards.access_notes: Event access varies; use the individual event page for registration and entry details.

cards.title: Walk across to 41 Cooper Square
cards.subtitle: Third Avenue between East 6th and East 7th Streets; entrance on East 7th Street
cards.notes: Use the walk to identify the School of Engineering building and gallery location, then save the entrance rules and building hours for future visits.
cards.short_summary: Cooper’s newer academic building across from the Foundation Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper lists 41 Cooper Square on Third Avenue between East 6th and East 7th Streets, with its entrance on East 7th Street.
cards.access_notes: Students need a current Cooper ID to enter academic buildings during posted hours.

cards.title: See what is on view at 41 Cooper Gallery
cards.subtitle: 41 Cooper Square, Third Avenue between East 6th and East 7th Streets
cards.notes: Check the exhibition calendar before heading in; student shows rotate, so use the listed dates and open hours to choose a visit.
cards.short_summary: A Cooper exhibition space with rotating student work.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper describes 41 Cooper Gallery as an artistic activity site and its current student calendar lists rotating exhibitions and their on-view hours.
cards.access_notes: Exhibition hours vary by show; verify the current calendar and campus-entry requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Browse student organizations
cards.subtitle: Office of Student Affairs activity directory
cards.notes: Choose one group that matches an existing interest, then use its official contact or Student Affairs information to learn how to participate.
cards.short_summary: A structured way to find peers through recognized campus groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper says student organizations offer students opportunities to meet people with similar interests and lists multiple organization categories.
cards.access_notes: Participation and meeting details are organization-specific; contact the group or Student Affairs.

cards.entity_name: Herb Lubalin Study Center of Design and Typography
cards.title: Book a design-archive visit
cards.subtitle: 41 Cooper Square
cards.notes: If design history interests you, request an appointment and arrive with a focused topic so staff can help you use the archive responsibly.
cards.short_summary: A design-history collection and archive available by appointment.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper says the Herb Lubalin Study Center preserves design history and makes its materials available to the professional and general public by appointment.
cards.access_notes: Materials are available by appointment; arrange access before traveling to the center.

cards.title: Make a Saturday reading stop at Ottendorfer Library
cards.subtitle: 135 Second Avenue, New York, NY 10003
cards.notes: Bring a book or project notes for a quiet neighborhood stop, and confirm the branch calendar before leaving campus for the walk.
cards.short_summary: A nearby NYPL branch with Saturday service.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL lists Ottendorfer Library at 135 Second Avenue and gives regular Saturday hours of 10 AM–5 PM.
cards.access_notes: Regular Saturday hours are 10 AM–5 PM; review holiday closings and current branch notices first.

cards.title: End with a Voices from the Great Hall listen
cards.subtitle: Cooper Union’s public digital archive
cards.notes: Pick one recording from the archive and use it as a short reset after the walk; save another speaker or program for later listening.
cards.short_summary: A free online archive of recordings made in Cooper’s Great Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper describes Voices from the Great Hall as a free public online archive of original sound and video recordings made in the Great Hall.
cards.source_title: Sam Waterston Hosts Voices from the Great Hall
cards.access_notes: Online access; select a recording directly from the archive’s public collection.

warnings: Campus entry and gallery/event access are conditional; confirm the current calendar, posted building hours, and ID requirements before visiting.
